title: Ordering Numbers to 1000
keyIdea: To compare two numbers up to 1000, line up the places and scan from the left: hundreds first, then tens, then ones. The first place where the digits differ decides. Record it with >, = or <, and order a set by doing the same scan.
familyTip: Write two house numbers or page numbers one above the other, ones under ones. Ask which place to check first, then which place decides. Try a tricky pair like 305 and 350, or 98 and 120.

visual.caption: Which symbol fits each pair? Drag the pair into >, = or <, or tap the pair then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap the place that decides on a hundreds, tens and ones chart, drag a symbol into the gap, then order four numbers onto a 0 to 1000 line.

kid: A three-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. In 412 the 4 means 4 hundreds.
Start on the left. If one number has more hundreds, it is the bigger one. You can stop there. 412 is bigger than 398, even though 9 and 8 look big.
If the hundreds are the same, they do not help. Move right and look at the tens. Then the ones if you need to.
A zero still holds a place. 305 has no tens, but 350 has 5 tens. So 305 is less than 350. 98 has no hundreds at all. Put its ones under the ones of 120 first. Then you can see 98 is less.
adult: Ages 7 to 8. CCSS 2.NBT.4: compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens and ones digits, using >, = and < symbols to record the results. National Curriculum Year 3 number and place value: compare and order numbers up to 1000.

The method is a left-to-right scan of aligned place-value columns. The first column where the digits differ decides the comparison, and every column to its right is irrelevant: 412 > 398 because 4 hundreds > 3 hundreds, regardless of 98 > 12. Ordering a set repeats the scan, grouping by hundreds and then by tens.

Common mistakes: letting the larger tens or ones digits win (calling 398 bigger than 412); treating numbers with the same digits as equal (305 and 350); ignoring a zero that holds a place; comparing the first digits of a two-digit and a three-digit number without aligning the places (98 vs 120, '9 > 1'); and turning the > or < sign the wrong way.

In the lab your child taps the column that decides on a chart of hundreds flats, tens rods and ones cubes, drags a symbol into the gap between 708 and 780, then drags 640, 604, 460 and 406 into order and sees them land on a 0 to 1000 number line.

practice.hint: Check the hundreds digit of each number before anything else.
practice.explain: 412 has 4 hundreds and 398 has 3 hundreds. More hundreds wins, so 412 > 398.

practice.hint: The hundreds match, so compare the tens. The zero means no tens.
practice.explain: Both have 3 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 5 tens, so 305 < 350.

practice.prompt: What number has {h} hundreds, {t} tens and {o} ones?
practice.hint: Each hundred is worth 100 and each ten is worth 10. Add the ones last.
Find the numbers with the fewest hundreds, then compare their tens.
practice.explain: 406 and 460 have 4 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 6 tens, so 406 is smallest.

practice.prompt: What is the hundreds digit of {=h*100+t*10+o}?
practice.hint: In a three-digit number the hundreds digit is the one on the left.
practice.explain: {=h*100+t*10+o} is {h} hundreds, {t} tens and {o} ones, so the hundreds digit is {h}.

pool.hint: 98 has no hundreds digit. Line up the ones before you compare.
pool.explain: 98 has 0 hundreds and 120 has 1 hundred, so 98 < 120.

pool.hint: Check every place: hundreds, tens and ones.
pool.explain: Every place matches (7 hundreds, 2 tens, 6 ones), so 726 = 726.

pool.hint: Same hundreds, so the tens decide. The open side faces the greater number.
pool.explain: Both have 7 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 8 tens, so 708 < 780.

pool.prompt: Sam says 398 > 412 because 9 and 8 are big digits. What went wrong?
choices: He used the wrong symbol only
pool.hint: Scan from the left. Which place differs first?
pool.explain: 3 hundreds is less than 4 hundreds, so 398 < 412. The tens and ones never get a say.

pool.hint: 100 more means the hundreds digit goes up by one. Tens and ones stay the same.
Two numbers have 5 hundreds. Compare their tens.
pool.explain: 563 and 536 both have 5 hundreds. 6 tens beat 3 tens, so 563 is greatest.

pool.prompt: What is the tens digit of {=h*100+t*10+o}?
pool.hint: The tens digit is the middle digit of a three-digit number.
pool.explain: {=h*100+t*10+o} has {t} tens, so the tens digit is {t}.

pool.prompt: Are 305 and 350 equal because they use the same digits?
pool.hint: Equal needs every place to match, not just the same digits.
pool.explain: The tens differ (0 and 5), so 305 < 350. Same digits in different places give different numbers.
